questions.question: On the bank of now dry course of which river, the ancient city of Harappa was built?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ravi**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The ancient city of **Harappa** was built on the bank of the now dry course of the **Ravi River**.
 
• Harappa is one of the most significant archaeological sites of the **Indus Valley Civilization**, located in modern-day Pakistan.
 
• The city is known for its advanced **urban planning, architecture, and social organization**.
 
• The Ravi River, which once flowed near Harappa, was crucial for the civilization's agriculture and trade.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Indus Valley Civilization** is one of the **world's oldest civilizations**, dating back to around **3300 BCE**.
 
• It was contemporary with the civilizations of** Mesopotamia and Ancient Egypt**.
 
• The civilization extended across what is now Pakistan and northwest India, and it is known for its well-planned cities like Harappa and Mohenjo-Daro.
 
• The decline of the Indus Valley Civilization is believed to have been caused by a combination of factors including climate change, river course changes, and possibly invasions.

questions.question: Which term is used to denote the mean income computed for every man, woman, and child in a particular group including those living in group quarters?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Per capita income**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Per capita income** is the term used to denote the mean income computed for every man, woman, and child in a particular group, including those living in group quarters.
 
• It is a measure of the **average income earned per person** in a given area in a specified year.
 
• This metric is used to compare the economic well-being of different populations or to track the economic progress of a region over time.
 
• Per capita income helps in understanding the **standard of living **and economic health of a population.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Per capita income** is calculated by dividing the total income of a particular area by its population.
 
• It is often used in economic studies and reports to provide a more accurate representation of individual prosperity than total income or GDP alone.
 
• While it is a useful measure, it does not account for income distribution within the population.
 
• Higher per capita income generally indicates a higher standard of living and better economic conditions.

questions.question: Kathak dance is known as combination of _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Music, dance and narrative**__

__
 
• **Kathak** is a classical dance form originating from northern India.
 
• It is known for its intricate **footwork, spins, and expressive gestures**.
 
• Kathak incorporates **music, dance, and narrative** elements to convey stories, often from ancient Indian epics and mythology.
 
• The narrative aspect of Kathak is delivered through **mime and facial expressions**, making it a unique blend of various artistic components.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The name **Kathak** is derived from the Sanskrit word **'Katha'** meaning story, and **'Kathakar'** meaning storyteller.
 
• Historically, Kathak dancers, known as **Kathakars**, used to travel and narrate stories through dance and music.
 
• The dance form evolved during the **Bhakti movement** and later under the patronage of Mughal rulers, which added Persian influences to its style.
 
• Kathak is one of the eight recognized classical dance forms of India, and it continues to be a popular performance art both in India and globally.

__
 
• **Jus soli** is a term that refers to the right of anyone born in the territory of a state to nationality or citizenship, which is not a writ issued by the Supreme Court of India.
 
• The writs issued by the Supreme Court of India include **Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Quo Warranto, and Certiorari**.
 
• The writ of **Habeas Corpus** is used to **secure the release of a person who has been unlawfully detained**.
 
• The writ of **Prohibition** is issued by a** higher court to a lower court to prevent it from exceeding its jurisdiction**.
 
• The writ of **Quo Warranto** is used to **challenge the legality of a person's claim to a public office**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The writ of **Mandamus** is issued by the court to **compel a public authority to perform its duty**.
 
• The writ of **Certiorari** is issued by a** higher court to a lower court to transfer a case for review**.
 
• These writs are a part of the judicial review mechanism in India to ensure the protection of fundamental rights.
 
• The power to issue these writs is vested in the Supreme Court under **Article 32** and in the High Courts under **Article 226** of the Constitution of India.
 
• These writs are essential tools to maintain the rule of law and to ensure that public authorities act within their legal bounds.

questions.question: The Simon Commission arrived in India in _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1928**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Simon Commission** arrived in India in **1928**.
 
• The Simon Commission was a group of **seven British Members of Parliament** that was sent to India in **1928 **to study constitutional reform.
 
• It was headed by **Sir John Simon** and was officially known as the** Indian Statutory Commission**.
 
• The commission faced strong protests from Indian leaders and the general public as it did not include any Indian members.
 
• The slogan "**Simon Go Back**" became popular during the protests against the commission.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Simon Commission was** appointed in 1927** and arrived in India in 1928.
 
• Its purpose was to review the working of the **Government of India Act 1919** and suggest further reforms.
 
• The **commission's report**, published in **1930**, led to the **Round Table Conference**s and eventually the **Government of India Act 1935**.
 
• The Government of India Act 1935 laid the foundation for the federal structure of India and introduced provincial autonomy.
 
• The Indian leaders' opposition to the Simon Commission highlighted the demand for greater self-governance and inclusion of Indians in decision-making processes.
